request.spec:
Pasted claims now arrive OPEN: after the lines are checked, each claim is added and then opened by
the signed-in user exactly as the open button would (numbered in paste order, writing CLAIM_ADDED
then CLAIM_OPENED with the rollup lines, going to REVIEW when that applies later), and any refusal
the open button would give (a note required, a period's cap, a flag, a permission) refuses the whole
paste. A line naming a person, date and note that match one of their claims as they stood before the
paste updates that claim instead of adding one (two lines of one paste never match each other, and
void or deleted claims never match): a DRAFT is edited to the line's amount (CLAIM_EDITED when it
changes) and opened, the newest such DRAFT when several match; a line whose matches include no DRAFT
is an error for the paste. Show how many lines went through.

agent.result_text:
Pasted claims now arrive open. `bin/e2e` builds and runs the app, and all 4 tests in the spec pass.

**Server (`paste/PasteService.java`)**
- Lines are still checked first, as before.
- Before adding anything, it takes a copy of the sheet's claims as they stand, leaving out void and deleted ones. Lines are matched against that copy only, so two lines of the same paste can't match each other.
- **No match:** the claim is added, which writes `CLAIM_ADDED`.
- **Matches a DRAFT:** it uses the newest matching DRAFT. If the amount differs it edits it through the normal edit path, which writes `CLAIM_EDITED`; if the amount is the same, nothing is written for the edit.
- **Matches only non-DRAFT claims:** the whole paste is refused, with an error naming the line.
- Every line's claim is then opened by the same code the open button uses. Lines are numbered in paste order, the rollup lines are written, and any refusal the open button gives (note required, period cap, flag, permission) refuses the whole paste. Because the paste is one transaction, a refusal stores nothing and writes nothing to the audit file.
- If a line leaves the date blank, it is matched on the date a new claim would get. I added a small public `ClaimService.addedOn(...)` for that, which uses the existing entry-date rule.

**Front end (`people/people.ts`)**: the button now reads "Open pasted claims", and the count is labelled "Went through". The `paste-added` count includes updated DRAFTs as well as new claims.

**Behaviours the request didn't spell out:**
- When a line matches a DRAFT, its ` #reference` (if it has one) is not applied; the DRAFT keeps its own reference and tags.
- Nothing in the code handles REVIEW yet, so the "going to REVIEW when that applies later" part needs no work now. Once that status exists, pastes will pick it up, since they open claims through the same path as the button.
